75-1267.caption_text:
LEWIS FARM

Early in the 1900's, as suggested by the many fine maples along the avenue, the property became known as "Maple Ridge" and also as "Maple Avenue Dairy Farm". Passing years found the names falling into disuse and it simply became known as the "Lewis Farm". Efforts are being made to re-establish the name "Maple Ridge".

This is a one family farm, title always having been vested in the Lewis family. Amos Lewis, first supervisor of the Town of Caton, purchased the land from Peter De Wolfe in 1833. In 1835, Christopher D. Lewis started acquiring the farm from his Uncle. The original development occurred during his ownership with the type of farming being typical for the day. Forest products, potatoes, fruit, dairy products and wool were marketed.

In 1899, the heirs of Christopher D. Lewis sold the farm to a grandson from Iowa, Anson C. Lewis. He moved his family and fine horses to Caton. In the 1920's, mechanization was undertaken and fields were enlarged, but dairying remained and the sheep operation was converted to a dairy farm. The place was one of the early ones to have a water system produced by a windmill, carbide lights, hot water heat and a bathroom.

In 1948, title was passed to a daughter, Sadie L. Crooker, by Anson C. Lewis. Ownership is still retained by her. Since about 1920, the farm has been operated as a dairy farm. Her husband, the late Walter C. Crooker and their sons. At the present writing, 1975, Curtis and Carley Crooker with an assist from their nephew, Curtis Cowles, are attempting to modernize and enlarge the dairy operation.

This is a brief history of a farm owned and operated continuously by the same family for 142 years.
